chunks: Then they pushed you into the hollows of disgrace, threw you into the whirlpools of slaughter, and trampled you, wounding you by striking your eyes with spears, cutting your throats, tearing your nostrils, breaking your limbs and taking you in ropes of control towards the fire already prepared. In this way he became more harmful to your religion and a greater kindler of flames (of mischief) about your worldly matters than the enemies against whom you showed open opposition and against whom you marched your forces.
ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about the causes of disgrace and slaughter for the believers?
ai.summary: In the context of the Khawarij's rebellion, Imam Ali uses this vivid imagery to illustrate how their external aggression was compounded by the internal political missteps of the Muslims, particularly the arbitration at Siffin. This passage highlights the Shia scholarly view that the 'greater wound' to the faith came not just from the enemy's sword, but from the believers' own hesitation and the rise of factions that turned against the Imamate, fulfilling the warning against vanity and Satan's influence.
